Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from the game. A convincing victory for the Sri Lanka Women Under-19 side. The action continues as we have a game lined up next between the India Women Under-19 and the hosts, Malaysia Women Under-19. The build up for the game has already started so do switch tabs and enjoy the coverage of that game. Cheers!

Manudi Nanayakkara, the skipper of Sri Lanka Women Under-19, says that she is happy and their team did really well. Adds that the coaching staff is hard working and their batters did very well. Ends by saying that they will carry on with the same momentum in their next game as well.

Samara Ramnath, the skipper of West Indies Women Under-19, says that it was a disappointing effort from their side. Adds that they will look to leave this behind and bounce back. Ends by saying that the next game is important for them.

Chamudi Praboda is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for her impressive showing with the ball. Mentions that she tries to be consistent with her lines and lengths and be as accurate as possible. Tells that she wants to end the competition as the leading-wicket taker and contribute to the team's cause.
Presentations coming up...

Earlier in the match, Sri Lanka, led by Sanjana Kavindi and captain Manudi Nanayakkara, took control after a shaky start. Although West Indies briefly increased the pressure by taking a few quick wickets in the middle overs, they couldn't sustain it. Sri Lanka finished with a record total of 166, surpassing their previous best of 162. West Indies struggled, conceding a record 36 extras and having issues with catching and ground fielding, despite starting well.

Chamudi Praboda was the standout performer for Sri Lanka Women Under-19, claiming 3 wickets to spearhead her team's dominant display and she was well supported by the other bowlers. They will look to carry on with the same momentum in their following games as well.

The few remaining hopes for West Indies Women Under-19 were crashed in the 9th over when Samara Ramnath was dismissed and they knew they couldn't make any comeback. Sri Lanka Women Under-19 excelled in all aspects of the game, showcasing exceptional bowling and fielding as well. They consistently broke partnerships, preventing the West Indies team from gaining any traction in their chase.

A dominant all round performance from the Sri Lanka Women Under-19! They defeat West Indies Women Under-19 by a convincing margin of 81 runs. The West Indies team faced a daunting task, chasing a substantial target, and their innings was marred by a rocky start. Despite a valiant effort from their skipper, Samara Ramnath, who seemed to be shouldering the responsibility alone, the team's batting lineup struggled and wickets kept falling at regular intervals.
